winner.title: Khorkhog (Mongolian Meat Cooked with Hot Stones)

evidence.authenticity: Sheep only, caraway/salt/pepper, milk-can vessel, stones passed around and rubbed; goat noted as variant. Mongolia-focused site but no named author.
evidence.precision: Water 3-5 dl, 10-20 fist-sized stones, stone heating about 1 hour. Meat amount vague ('0.5-1 p.'), vegetables 3-6 kg, seasoning unmeasured, no fixed cook time (judged by sound and smell), no vessel size.
evidence.testing: Explains steam from water, stone heat plus stove heat, pressure-lock warning, stones turning glossy black as a doneness sign. No test-kitchen process.
evidence.photos: About 11 step photos: meat cut, fire, stones in can, closed can, open can, finished dish.
evidence.efficiency: Stones heat while prep happens; no wasted steps, but no stated total time.
evidence.access: Lamb or goat and river stones are obtainable; two stacked pots work as a vessel. No subs needed beyond goat or lamb.

winner.why: Most traditional and best illustrated of the pages read, but the vague quantities and timing keep it just under 60.

runnerUp.title: Mongolian Khorkhog

evidence.authenticity: Learned from nomadic families; goat with ribs, potatoes, carrots, stones passed around.
evidence.precision: Metric quantities (5 kg goat, 300 ml water, 10-15 stones) but no doneness cues, no pan size, only 'cook 1.5 hours'.
evidence.photos: Photos of cooking with a nomadic family and stones among the meat.
evidence.efficiency: Stones heated while prepping; 5 kg batch is impractical for home.
evidence.access: Goat can be swapped for mutton or lamb.

runnerUp.why: Clear steps and context, but time-only cooking, an oversized batch and no doneness cues.

candidates.disqualified: Near-verbatim copy of the Nomadic Boys recipe; no process photos in schema
No ingredient amounts; wok, white wine, honey and lemon make it an adaptation
